## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vālodakajātaka* (Ja 183) is a canonical Pali Jātaka tale belonging to the *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In modern English translations, it is known by titles such as *A Nasty Drink*  or categorized under the theme of sobriety [Anandajoti 2010]. The verse opening begins with the hemistich *Vālodakaṁ apparasaṁ nihīnaṁ* [Fausböll 1879].

According to the traditional frame story set at Jetavana, the Buddha relates the tale concerning five hundred scrap-eaters (*vighāsāda*) or vagabonds allowed to reside within the monastery precinct who behaved undisciplinedly [Burlingame 1921a; Fausböll 1879]. The narrative contrasts noble, well-trained Sindh war-horses who drink high-quality liquor without losing their composure with lowly donkeys who become wildly drunk and disorderly after ingesting merely the strained, sour dregs (*vālodaka*) [Burlingame 1921b; Anandajoti 2010]. The Buddha uses the analogy to illustrate that well-born, virtuous men practice renunciation and remain undisturbed in the face of joy or sorrow, whereas uncultivated persons quickly become unrestrained [Burlingame 1921b].
